name: hated-wow-mcp

tools.name: wow_api_search
tools.description: Search World of Warcraft's in-game Lua API — the functions an addon can call from inside the client. Covers namespaced functions (C_Item.GetItemInfo), legacy globals (UnitHealth), and widget methods (Frame:SetPoint). Results include full argument and return signatures. Use this before writing any addon code that calls the game.

query.description: Function name or fragment. Matches exact names, prefixes, substrings and camel-hump abbreviations (GIIBID finds GetItemInfoByID).

flavor.description: Game client to answer for. Defaults to WOW_DEFAULT_FLAVOR, or retail.

namespace.description: Restrict to one namespace, e.g. C_Spell.

tools.name: wow_api_event_search
tools.description: Search the events an addon can register with frame:RegisterEvent, and show each event's payload arguments in order. Use this whenever writing an OnEvent handler, so the argument list matches what the client sends.

query.description: Event name or fragment, e.g. COMBAT_LOG or BAG_UPDATE.

flavor.description: Game client to answer for. Defaults to WOW_DEFAULT_FLAVOR, or retail.

tools.name: wow_api_type_search
tools.description: Search the Enum.*, Constants.* and structure tables the in-game API uses — for example Enum.ItemQuality or the AuraData structure returned by C_UnitAuras. Searching for a member name finds the table that contains it.

query.description: Type, enum, constant or member name.

flavor.description: Game client to answer for. Defaults to WOW_DEFAULT_FLAVOR, or retail.

kind.description: Restrict to one kind of table.

tools.name: wow_api_diff
tools.description: Check whether a function, event or type exists in each game client (retail, Classic progression, Classic Era, WoW Forever). Use this before writing code that has to run on more than one flavor, or to explain why something works on Classic but not retail.

name.description: Function, event or type name, e.g. GetSpellInfo or C_Item.GetItemInfo.

tools.name: wow_api_stats
tools.description: Report which API index, UI source and game data sets this server has, when each was synced, and how large it is. Use this to confirm the data is present and current before relying on other tools.

tools.name: wow_ui_template_search
tools.description: Search the virtual XML templates that ship with the game — the frames an addon can inherit by name to get Blizzard's own look and behaviour (buttons, scroll lists, panels, tooltips). Shows the inheritance chain, attached mixins and where each is defined. Use this instead of writing frame art from scratch.

query.description: Template name or fragment, e.g. ScrollBox or UIPanelButton.

type.description: Restrict to an element type, e.g. Button, Frame, CheckButton.

tools.name: wow_ui_mixin_search
tools.description: Search the mixin tables Blizzard's UI uses — reusable method sets attached to frames via the XML mixin attribute or CreateFromMixins. Searching a method name finds the mixin that defines it. Use this to reuse Blizzard's behaviour or to understand what a template's methods do.

query.description: Mixin name, fragment, or an exact method name.

tools.name: wow_cvar_search
tools.description: Find the game's console variables — the settings behind SetCVar/GetCVar. Covers every CVar the client registers, and for the ones Blizzard's own UI touches, shows how it reads them, where, and what the options screen calls them. Use this before writing SetCVar, or to discover which CVar controls a piece of game behaviour.

query.description: CVar name or fragment, e.g. nameplate, cameraDistance.

usedOnly.description: Only CVars Blizzard's own UI reads or writes — the documented-by-example ones.

tools.name: wow_ui_grep
tools.description: Regex-search the full Lua and XML source of the 348 Blizzard addons that ship with the client. This is the ground truth for how the game itself does something — event handling, secure frames, data providers, layout. Use it when the API reference tells you what a function is but not how it is meant to be used.

pattern.description: JavaScript regular expression to search for.

pkg.description: Restrict to one Blizzard package, e.g. Blizzard_ActionBar.

context.description: Lines of surrounding context per hit.

tools.name: wow_ui_read_file
tools.description: Read a Lua or XML file from Blizzard's shipped interface source, by the path that wow_ui_grep or wow_ui_template_search reported. Use this to see a full implementation in context rather than a single matching line.

path.description: Path relative to the UI source root, e.g. Interface/AddOns/Blizzard_UIParent/UIParent.lua.

tools.name: wow_ui_list_packages
tools.description: List the Blizzard_* addon packages that ship with the client, optionally filtered. Use this to find which package owns a piece of the UI before grepping it, e.g. Blizzard_ActionBar for action buttons.

filter.description: Substring filter on the package name.

tools.name: wow_lua_lint
tools.description: Analyse addon Lua for problems specific to World of Warcraft: APIs that were removed or moved into a namespace in the target client, unknown events, taint (calling protected functions, overwriting Blizzard globals, touching secure frames in combat), and performance traps. Run this on any addon Lua before shipping it, and whenever porting between clients.

path.description: Path to a .lua file to analyse instead of inline code.

knownGlobals.description: Globals defined elsewhere (embedded libraries, other files) — suppresses unknown-API warnings for them.

tools.name: wow_xml_validate
tools.description: Validate WoW interface XML against Blizzard's own UI.xsd: unknown or misspelled elements and attributes, invalid nesting, bad enum values, and structural mistakes like a virtual frame with no name. Run this on every XML file an addon loads — the client silently ignores what it does not understand, so these mistakes are otherwise invisible.

path.description: Path to a .xml file to validate.

tools.name: wow_toc_validate
tools.description: Validate a .toc manifest: interface version against the target client, flavor suffix consistency, unrecognised directives the client silently drops, SavedVariables names, and files listed but missing (or present but unlisted). Run this whenever an addon fails to load or shows as out of date.

path.description: Path to a .toc file, or to an addon folder.

fileName.description: Filename to assume when validating inline contents, e.g. MyAddon_Vanilla.toc.

tools.name: wow_addon_scaffold
tools.description: Generate a complete, working addon skeleton: .toc manifests for the chosen clients, an event-dispatch Core.lua with SavedVariables handling and a slash command, and optionally an XML frame template with its Lua mixin and a Settings-API options panel. Use this to start a new addon rather than writing boilerplate by hand. By default it only returns the files. With `write` it saves them into the addon folder, and it refuses if any of the files already exist unless `overwrite` is also set.

name.description: Addon name; also the folder name.

flavors.description: Clients to support. Defaults to retail only.

notes.description: One-line description for the .toc and README.

slashCommand.description: Slash command without the leading slash.

withFrame.description: Include an XML template and frame mixin.

withOptions.description: Include a Settings API options panel.

write.description: Write the files into the configured addon folder instead of just returning them.

overwrite.description: With `write`, replace files that already exist. Off by default: scaffolding a name that matches an installed addon would otherwise silently replace its real files.

tools.name: wow_install_info
tools.description: Report the World of Warcraft installations found on this machine — their paths, flavors, build numbers, and the addons currently installed. Use this to confirm which client tools will target and to discover addon folders to lint.

tools.name: wow_file_search
tools.description: Find game art and asset files by name, and get the FileDataID and texture path an addon needs to reference them. Covers every interface texture and icon (and models and maps when the full index is synced). A numeric query is treated as a FileDataID and resolved back to its path. Use this whenever writing SetTexture, SetNormalTexture or SetModel.

query.description: File name fragment, or a numeric FileDataID to resolve.

under.description: Restrict to a path prefix, e.g. interface/icons/ or interface/buttons/.

ext.description: Restrict by extension, e.g. blp or m2.

includeNonInterface.description: Search beyond interface/** — models, maps, sounds. Requires the full index.

tools.name: wow_icon_search
tools.description: Search the game's icon textures by name and return the path and FileDataID for each. Icons follow a naming convention (spell_fire_*, inv_sword_*, ability_warrior_*), so searching by theme works well. Use this to pick an icon for a button, an addon compartment entry, or a .toc IconTexture.

query.description: Icon name fragment, e.g. fireball, sword, warrior.

tools.name: wow_atlas_search
tools.description: Search the named texture atlas elements the UI uses with SetAtlas, the modern way to reference Blizzard art, since an atlas name carries its own size and coordinates. Returns dimensions, the sheet FileDataID and the exact SetAtlas call. Prefer atlases over raw texture paths for UI art. Atlases differ between clients, so name the flavor you are writing for: an atlas that exists on retail may not exist on WoW Forever or Classic.

tools.name: wow_data_status
tools.description: Report which game data sets are synced — the file/FileDataID index and the texture atlas index — with counts and sync dates, and what to run for any that are missing. Use this when a game data lookup returns nothing.

tools.name: wow_model_search
tools.description: Find M2 (creature, doodad, prop) and WMO (building, dungeon) models in the game's listfile by path fragment, or resolve a numeric FileDataID. Returns the FileDataID and path to pass to wow_model_export. Needs the game-data sync.

query.description: Words that appear in the path, e.g. 'thunder bluff' or 'cairne', or a FileDataID.

tools.name: wow_model_export
tools.description: Export a model from the local WoW install's game files into a folder, headless. M2 models become glTF with animations (or GLB/OBJ); WMO models become OBJ+MTL (or glTF). Textures are decoded to PNG beside the model in the game's folder layout, so relative texture paths resolve in Blender. The first call opens the game storage and takes about 30 seconds. Needs the game-data and model-data syncs.

outputDir.description: Folder to write into (created if missing).

format.description: Default: gltf for M2, obj for WMO.

animations.description: Include animations for M2 glTF. Default true.

splitGroups.description: WMO OBJ: one object per group.

flavor.description: Which installed client to read: mainline (retail), forever, classic or vanilla. Defaults to the first install found.

tools.name: wow_creature_search
tools.description: Find creatures and NPCs by name (or creature id, or display id) in the local game files, with the model each one uses. Opens the game storage, so the first call takes about 40 seconds. Use the id with wow_creature_export.

query.description: Creature name fragment, creature id or display id.

flavor.description: Which installed client to read: mainline (retail), forever, classic or vanilla. Defaults to the first install found.

tools.name: wow_creature_export
tools.description: Export a creature or NPC as glTF with animations and its skin textures, headless. Beasts and monsters get their display skin and geosets. Humanoid NPCs (built from a player race model) get the right race and sex model, the NPC's hair, beard and similar geosets, and the baked NPC skin; worn gear is not applied yet. Written to <outputDir>/creatures/.

displayId.description: Display id, when there is no creature id.

outputDir.description: Folder to write into (created if missing).

flavor.description: Which installed client to read: mainline (retail), forever, classic or vanilla. Defaults to the first install found.

tools.name: wow_texture_export
tools.description: Decode a BLP texture from the local WoW install to PNG, keeping the game's folder layout under outputDir. Accepts a FileDataID or listfile path.

texture.description: FileDataID or listfile path of a .blp.

outputDir.description: Folder to write into (created if missing).

flavor.description: Which installed client to read: mainline (retail), forever, classic or vanilla. Defaults to the first install found.

tools.name: wow_map_search
tools.description: Find maps (continents, instances, battlegrounds) by name, directory or id in the local game files. Also converts a world position to the terrain tile that holds it. Opens the game storage, so the first call takes about 40 seconds.

query.description: Map name fragment, directory (e.g. 'Kalimdor') or map id.

x.description: World x (north) to find the tile for.

y.description: World y (west) to find the tile for.

flavor.description: Which installed client to read: mainline (retail), forever, classic or vanilla. Defaults to the first install found.

tools.name: wow_map_export
tools.description: Export terrain tiles of a map as OBJ with a texture, headless. Give a map id from wow_map_search plus tiles, or a world position. Texture modes: 'tex0' blends the tile's layers into one PNG (default), 'alpha' writes the layer textures and blend masks, 'none' is geometry only. Optionally places the tile's buildings and props. Written to <outputDir>/maps/<directory>/. Baked high-resolution textures are not supported (they need a GPU).

tiles.description: Tile pairs [a, b] from the file name map_a_b.adt.

x.description: World x (north); with y, picks the tile.

outputDir.description: Folder to write into (created if missing).

objects.description: Also export the tile's WMO and M2 placements. Slow.

flavor.description: Which installed client to read: mainline (retail), forever, classic or vanilla. Defaults to the first install found.

instructions:
This server exposes World of Warcraft addon development knowledge: the
in-game Lua API, Blizzard's own shipped UI source, and the game's art and
file data.

Guidance:
  - Check wow_api_search before writing any call into the game. The API
    differs per client and moves between patches; do not rely on memory.
  - Use wow_ui_grep and wow_ui_template_search to see how Blizzard itself
    implements a piece of UI before building it from scratch.
  - Run wow_lua_lint on addon Lua before considering it finished. It
    catches removed APIs and taint problems that only appear at runtime.
  - Reference art through wow_file_search / wow_atlas_search rather than
    guessing texture paths; a wrong path fails silently in-game.
